designSummary: Single-arm feasibility pilot judged against pre-specified progression criteria; no hypothesis tests.
sampleSize: Six practices produce about 3,000 HbA1c requests in four months (about 96,000 a year across 64 practices). With 18 percent early requests, about 540 holds are expected; with about 11 percent overridden (c3), about 60 overrides. If 90 percent are completed within one working day, 60 overrides give a 95 percent confidence interval of about 82 to 98 percent, enough to tell whether the threshold is plausibly met. Zero important delays among about 540 holds would put the upper 95 percent bound for the delay rate near 0.6 percent (rule of three).
primaryAnalysis: Proportion of overrides for accepted exceptions completed within one working day with a Wilson 95 percent confidence interval, compared descriptively with the 90 percent threshold.
secondaryAnalysis: Firing and override rates by practice and month; override reasons; safety review counts with the rule-of-three bound; acceptability proportion; second draws.
missingData: Overrides without a recorded time are reported as not timely in a sensitivity count; unreturned surveys are reported by practice and role.
multiplicity: Progression criteria are judged together as pre-specified; no significance testing.
software: Laboratory information system extracts summarised in R.
overfittingGuards: No post hoc change of the 80-day interval during the pilot
summary: About 60 overrides and 540 holds; interval estimates against fixed thresholds.
